clips.title: Monorepos - How the Pros Scale Huge Software Projects // Turborepo vs Nx
clips.why: Two of our repos are monorepos: fcp holds the whole product, and ai-agents holds every platform service as an npm workspace. This is a fast, clear look at what that buys you and what it costs.
look: The benefits: one place for shared code, and one change that can touch several packages at once.
The problem he names: a monorepo needs tooling, or every build and test runs everything.
npm workspaces: the feature that links the packages of one repo together, which ai-agents uses.
clips.after: fcp and ai-agents are each one monorepo, but they are separate repos from each other, so a change that touches both is two pull requests.

clips.title: Terraform in 100 Seconds
clips.why: The infrastructure repo is written in OpenTofu, the open-source version of Terraform, so this is the quickest picture of what lives in that repo.
look: Infrastructure described in code: you write the resources you want, and the tool works out how to create them.
The plan and apply steps: first see what would change, then make the change.
clips.after: In our infrastructure repo a person always runs plan and apply; an agent never does, and DevOps approves every change.

clips.title: What is GitOps, How GitOps works and Why it's so useful
clips.why: Our gitops repo is exactly what Nana describes, so this clip explains what that repo is for, and why our agent services are deployed a different way.
look: GitOps: a Git repo is the single place that describes what runs in a cluster.
The pull model: a tool such as Argo CD inside the cluster pulls changes from the repo.
The push model: a pipeline or a person pushes the change into the cluster.
clips.after: The product clusters use the pull model through the gitops repo. Our agent services on inf are installed from the infrastructure repo, when a person runs the apply.

practice.q: A ticket's sketch path is cloud/rhinoCloud/tests_api/builders.py. Which repo is it?

options.why: ai-agents paths start with a workspace such as broker/ or harness/, and its code is TypeScript.
cloud/ is the product's Django backend, one of fcp's top folders.
infrastructure's top folders are modules/, terraform/, multi_tenant/ and packer/.

practice.q: A change needs a new field in ai-agents and a matching change in fcp. Can one Nova run do both?

options.text: Yes, if the plan lists both files.
options.why: The plan cannot widen the run's token. The broker gives each run a token for one repo.

options.text: No: each run gets a token for exactly one repo, so it becomes two tickets and two pull requests.
options.why: One repo per run keeps a fooled run from reaching further than the one place it was given.

options.text: Yes, because both repos belong to RhinoHealth.
options.why: Being in the same organisation does not matter. The token names one repo.

practice.q: Complete the title so it follows our format: the owning team in brackets, then the deliverable.
practice.after: ] Broker: git proxy that checks repo and branch before pushing
practice.hint: The team that builds the agent platform itself.
practice.why: The team in brackets tells you who owns the ticket before you read anything else.

practice.q: Put the parts of a ticket in the order you read them.
items: The title: the team in brackets and what it delivers
What: what gets built or decided
Why: what goes wrong without it
How: the practical steps, with real paths and names
The code sketch: the shape of the key file and its path
practice.why: The title and What tell you what exists afterwards, the Why tells you what problem it removes, and the How and the sketch are the route. Reading the sketch first tempts you to copy code before you know why.

practice.q: Which of these is a well-written ticket title?

options.why: Nobody knows who owns it or what it delivers.

options.text: [Platform] Broker: one Jira issue, one Slack thread, artifacts, audit log
options.why: Team in brackets, a concrete deliverable, under 75 characters.

options.text: It would be good if Nova could talk to Jira and Slack safely without holding any tokens on its machine
options.why: Too long, no team, and it describes a wish instead of something that will exist.

practice.q: Why is the agent platform's repo called ai-agents and not agents?

options.text: In the product, agent already means the Rhino Client that runs at customer sites.
options.why: rhinoAgent and rhino-agent-qa-1 already exist, so everything about AI agents is called ai-agents to avoid confusion.

options.text: GitHub does not allow a repo called agents.
options.why: Any name works on GitHub. The reason is a name clash inside our own product.

options.text: To show that the repo is written in Python.
options.why: The platform is TypeScript. Only evals/ inside it is Python.
